correctness.rationale: The image-occupancy argument is quantified for arbitrary n>=2 and shows every proper image has a singleton level. A deterministic beat-deletion argument contracts any such image. Minimal-space rigidity then separates all homeomorphisms. The dependency-free verifier exhaustively checks n=1,2,3, including every self-map and every proper image.

originality.rationale: The checked primary sources supply the sphere models, minimal-space rigidity, and function-space framework, but not the all-dimensional ordinary self-homotopy classification. Prior related results are weaker after realization or cover only the n=1 boundary case. published-finding corpus and web searches returned no equivalent or dominating statement.
residual_risks: The 1966 Stong paper is foundational and directly relevant to finite-space homotopy, but its publisher PDF was inaccessible in this run. The exact rigidity fact used is explicitly restated in Barmak--Minian full text; an unlocated stronger self-map classification in Stong remains a bibliographic risk.
The full text of the 2002 Hardie--Vermeulen--Witbooi paper was unavailable; its accessible abstract does not state the present theorem.
Search failure is not a proof of novelty; the originality PASS rests on statement-level comparison of the inspected sources and prior claims, with these access risks disclosed.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a closed all-dimensional classification of ordinary self-homotopy classes of the canonical finite sphere models. It is structurally stronger than induced-degree information and shows a concrete mismatch between finite-space homotopy and weak sphere realization. This is a natural mapping-space invariant, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
